source.codes: tariffario_MOSCA_2024.xlsx!Foglio1!B3:H3 (column headers of the price table)
source.code_to_name_mapping: (inferred) by initials and by order: the image shows the classes left to right in the same order as columns B..H

fit_rule.statement: A pallet fits a class when weight_kg <= max_weight_kg AND height_cm <= max_height_cm AND its footprint is within 100 x 120 cm.
fit_rule.inclusive_limits: (inferred) the image states maxima ('Peso kg 150', 'Altezza 60 cm'); treat the limits as inclusive
fit_rule.footprint_rule: (inferred) every class shows 100 x 120 cm; an EPAL 80 x 120 fits; longer or wider loads are outside the classes (unknown how they are priced)
fit_rule.weight_basis: (inferred) real gross weight of the single pallet; the sheet does not apply a volumetric weight to pallet classes

selection_rule: A pallet usually fits several classes and prices are not monotonic across classes: charge the CHEAPEST fitting class for the destination region (see 07-pricing.md section 3). No class fits above 1200 kg or above 240 cm: manual quote.

covers.definition: [A, B] means class A allows at least the weight AND at least the height of class B, so every pallet that fits B also fits A

incomparable_pairs.definition: neither class covers the other: one is heavier, the other taller

not_a_total_order: ULP (350 kg, 240 cm) is taller but lighter than ELP (450 kg, 150 cm) and HP (600 kg, 150 cm). The column order B..H is therefore not a size order, and 'first fitting column' is not a valid selection rule.
naming_conflict: The new public site uses footprint names: 'EPAL / EUR 120 × 80 cm', 'Industriale 120 × 100 cm', 'Mezzo pallet 80 × 60 cm', 'Quarto di pallet 60 × 40 cm' (ls-home@claude/determined-lovelace-ggeitw:public/preventivo/index.html:225-228). 'Half Pallet' (HP) and 'Quarter Pallet' (QP) here are weight/height classes on a 100 x 120 cm base, not the 80 x 60 / 60 x 40 footprints.
